classification.difficultyReason: The exception is explicitly identified in the question; the student supplies one plausible contextual factor explaining why study time does not determine every individual mark.

content.prompt:
The scatterplot shows the study time and test mark of 10 students.

Why might a student who studied for more hours have a lower test mark than a student who studied for fewer hours?

spec.description: Scatterplot of study time against test mark for ten students, with offset arrowed axes, a pale grid and blue circular points.
spec.answerVisibility: All plotted points are permanent supplied givens.

answer.short: The student who studied for longer might have found the topic harder.
answer.worked: Students who study for longer tend to have higher marks, but there are exceptions. The student who studied for longer might have found the topic harder, so their mark can still be lower.
